home.summary: Privacy of the home and property are guaranteed by the Federal Constitution.

properties.explanation: Privacy of the home and property are guaranteed by the Federal Constitution.
Restrictions need a legal basis, a public interest and proportionality.

representative.note: The people in a home decide for themselves; representation does not apply.

individual.summary: Personal liberty, privacy and property are guaranteed by the Federal Constitution.

properties.explanation: Right to personal freedom, privacy and property.
Restrictions need a legal basis, a public interest and proportionality.

business.summary: People can start a business and govern it themselves through the owners' meeting and the managers they elect.

properties.explanation: Anyone may start and run a business.
Licensing and permit regimes restrict entry into many activities.
The content of a contract may be freely set within the law.

Mandatory rules fix some terms whatever both parties want: tenancy protections, cantonal minimum wages, and consumer terms that cannot be waived. Rules against fraud and coercion protect consent and are not counted.
Partners in a general or limited partnership, or members of a GmbH, decide together (partners' resolutions, members' meeting).
Its resolutions bind the company.
Owners decide the company's statutes, profits and leadership.
The partnership or company controls its own capital and income.
Shareholders of an AG decide in the general meeting (Generalversammlung).
Its resolutions bind the company.
Owners decide the company's statutes, profits and leadership.
The company controls its own capital and income.
Members of a cooperative (Genossenschaft) decide in its general meeting, one member one vote.
Its resolutions bind the company.
Members decide the statutes, the use of any surplus and the board.
The cooperative controls its own capital and income.
Owners elect the managers or board.
Managers and board members are elected individually.
The owners can dismiss them.
Anyone may authorise another to act for them (agency and mandate); a business may appoint a Prokurist.
The principal chooses the agent.
A mandate may be revoked at any time.
The agent must account for their conduct and hand over what they received.
The agent must carry out the mandate faithfully and with care.
Swiss law has no trusts of its own; foreign trusts are recognised, and fiduciary management is done under a mandate.
Under a fiduciary mandate the client chooses the fiduciary.
A fiduciary mandate may be revoked at any time.
The fiduciary must account to the client.
The fiduciary must act faithfully in the client's interest.

nonprofit.summary: People can form non-profit associations and foundations and govern them through a members' assembly and an elected board.

properties.explanation: People may freely form associations and foundations.
Registration and, for public-benefit status, supervision by the state.
Members decide in a general assembly.
Its decisions bind the organisation.
Members adopt the statutes and elect the board.
Funded by members, donors and grants; tax relief depends on public-benefit status.
The members elect a board.
The members can dismiss the board.

building.summary: Condominium owners decide in an owners' assembly and appoint an administrator. If the first meeting lacks a quorum, a second one needs only a third of owners.

properties.explanation: The assembly of condominium owners decides on joint administration.
Half of the owners holding half of the shares (and at least two) must attend; a second meeting, at least ten days later, needs one third.
Owners representing one fifth can demand a meeting (association law applies by reference).
Owners decide on contributions and the renewal fund.
The assembly appoints an administrator, who normally convenes and chairs it.
The assembly can dismiss the administrator.

entrance.summary: No separate regime per entrance; the building's owners' assembly decides.

union.summary: Switzerland is not a member of the European Union.

country.summary: Binding federal referendums and initiatives with no turnout quorum and modest signature thresholds. The National Council is elected from open lists per canton.

properties.explanation: If accepted by people and cantons, it becomes part of the Constitution.
It may be a general proposal or a fully worded draft.
100,000 signatures within 18 months.
A majority of those voting decides (plus a majority of cantons for constitutional changes).
Voters decide on the adopted text of the act.
50,000 signatures within 100 days, about 1% of voters.
Amendments to the Federal Constitution and joining supranational communities go to a vote automatically (Art. 140).
No petition is needed: constitutional amendments go to a vote automatically.
Open lists: voters can strike, add and cumulate individual candidates.
Each canton is a constituency.

state.summary: Cantonal initiative and referendum with low signature thresholds and no quorum, including a financial referendum on large spending.

properties.explanation: As a general suggestion or a fully worded draft.
6,000 signatures.
The vote is on the adopted act itself.
3,000 signatures within 60 days.
Amendments to the cantonal constitution, among others, go to a vote automatically.
No petition is needed: constitutional amendments go to a vote automatically.
180 members.
Including the cantonal tax rate.
Proportional representation with open lists.
The districts (Bezirke) are the constituencies.
Seven members elected by the people by majority vote.
No recall of elected officials at this level.

county.summary: Districts (Bezirke) mainly supervise the municipalities; they have no popular votes.

properties.explanation: A district (Bezirk) has no referendum.
A district (Bezirk) has no referendum.
A district (Bezirk) has no referendum.
Mostly supervisory and administrative powers.
No recall of elected officials at this level.

municipality.summary: Binding city initiatives and referendums with low signature thresholds and no quorum; big spending goes to a mandatory vote. The council is elected from open lists in nine districts. The tax rate is excluded from referendums.

properties.explanation: 3,000 signatures.
Optional referendum on council decisions; mandatory votes on the charter and on big spending.
The vote is on the adopted act itself.
2,000 signatures within 60 days.
Changes to the municipal charter and large expenditures go to a vote automatically.
No petition is needed: such decisions go to a vote automatically.
125 members.
Including setting the annual tax rate.
Proportional representation with open lists.
The city sets its own tax rate (Steuerfuss).
Nine members including the mayor, elected by the whole city.
No recall of elected officials at this level.

neighbourhood.summary: Quarters have no general decision-making body; quarter associations are private. Residents do elect a school board for their school district (covering several quarters), and council members per electoral district.

properties.explanation: A city district (Kreis) has no referendum of its own.
A city district (Kreis) has no referendum of its own.
A city district (Kreis) has no referendum of its own.
The charter provides no elected quarter or Kreis council.
Each of the seven school districts elects a school board (president plus 24 members).
Only for public schools and kindergartens in the district.
Members and president are elected by the district's voters.
The school district is the constituency; it spans several quarters.
Open lists: voters choose individual candidates.
Elected per electoral district (Wahlkreis), which is larger than one quarter.
